Pasting when there was nothing copied creates an action named "Set category/group \<null\>".

Also, the fact that the paste action in the popup uses "category" or "group" in the name is odd since "Paste Group Values" will actually paste a category if that's what you have copied. It should just be "Paste Copied Values" instead.

> Pasting when there was nothing copied creates an action named "Set category/group <null>".
> 
> Also, the fact that the paste action in the popup uses "category" or "group" in the name is odd since "Paste Group Values" will actually paste a category if that's what you have copied. It should just be "Paste Copied Values" instead.

I think copying properties from a category and pasting them into a group within that category should only paste the group's properties. This allows you to paste multiple groups within a single category without having to copy each group individually.

But if the properties of a category are pasted into a group that is in another category, nothing should happen.
Feature seems to be working well. Those commits need to be squashed, however.

I found unexpected behavior when pasting on multiple nodes.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c051e8f1-cc1f-48e5-bc36-6732443de4e4
> I found unexpected behavior when pasting on multiple nodes. > Screen.Recording.2025-10-13.130423.mp4 Could this come from the way I'm doing the undo/redo ?
The undo/redo usage looks correct, but for some reason it creates "Set category" as global action and makes individual action for each property. Something is wrong.

Ok I see what's the problem, but fixing it will involve modifying MultiNodeEdit.
MultiNodeEdit has undo/redo built-in in its `_set()` method. If you call `add_do_property()` on it, the undo action will cause another undo action. MultiNodeEdit itself is not recognized as part of the scene, hence there is history mismatch on to of that.

This is a bit messy, so I think you can just put a big FIXME comment and I will do a follow-up PR once this is merged.

EDIT:
Actually I came up with how to implement it independently. I will open a fix later today.

I realized it's wrong either way. You can't undo a property change on all nodes at once, because MultINodeEdit can't retrieve current value from all nodes, it will just use the first node. So if you want proper undo/redo, you will need to manually set properties on each node.

> I realized it's wrong either way. You can't undo a property change on all nodes at once, because MultINodeEdit can't retrieve current value from all nodes, it will just use the first node. So if you want proper undo/redo, you will need to manually set properties on each node.

What approach should I take then ?

Check if `object` is MultiNodeEdit, and if so, loop over its nodes and set properties individually.

You might need to do the same for EditorDebuggerRemoteObjects.

I think the feature is operational. However, it would be better to disable the paste buttons (like graying them out) if the clipboard doesn’t contain “@pastebin_category_name” or “@pastebin_section_name”, or if the category or section name doesn’t match.

Does not seem to work on ShaderMaterial

> Does not seem to work on ShaderMaterial It's not working with ShaderMaterial parameters and TileSet editor (and probably other sub resources with custom inspector). This happens because for some reason the editor path isn't the same as the inspector path (that is parsed in the _collect_properties function). I have no idea where to look to fix this, do you have an idea @KoBeWi ?

AtlasTileProxyObject inserts custom categories via `_get_property_list()`. This seems to be the problem. The AtlasTileProxyObject itself doesn't show as a category in the inspector, because it's empty; all properties are under a custom category.

The section does setup here
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/2af785641ae249573f45eb61852d22e0b1a8a03c/editor/inspector/editor_inspector.cpp#L4623
which includes setting the inspector path (the `doc_name` is assigned, because the proxy object category is parsed, even if it's empty).

> AtlasTileProxyObject inserts custom categories via `_get_property_list()`. This seems to be the problem. The AtlasTileProxyObject itself doesn't show as a category in the inspector, because it's empty; all properties are under a custom category.
> 
> The section does setup here
> 
> https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/2af785641ae249573f45eb61852d22e0b1a8a03c/editor/inspector/editor_inspector.cpp#L4623
> 
> which includes setting the inspector path (the `doc_name` is assigned, because the proxy object category is parsed, even if it's empty).

I have made a fix for the shader parameters by modifying this line. But for the TileSet I don't know if it needs to be fixed here or during the creation of the category / group.

My guess would be to fix it during the creation of the AtlasTileProxyObject category
I made a fix, see the above PR.

> I made a fix, see the above PR. I wonder if it'll be possible to copy paste sections that are exactly the same except for underscore suffixes at the end. In the material below, Material A & B has the exact same uniform naming convention, just with different "_A" & "_B" suffix.
I'm not sure there is a reliable way to detect and trim such prefixes.

> > I made a fix, see the above PR. > > I wonder if it'll be possible to copy paste sections that are exactly the same except for underscore suffixes at the end. In the material below, Material A & B has the exact same uniform naming convention, just with different "_A" & "_B" suffix. > I guess a way to do this would be to only get the section name and not the editor path to it. The issue with that is you can past properties to a section with the same name but not the same properties. It will not prevent you to copy and paste, but nothing will happen which I think is not really great for UX. A way to avoid this issue would be to enable the paste button only if at least one property of the same name is present in the section. Something like: Here you copy the section "Color" And then you passed onto another group of the same name. But only alpha will be pasted.

Does the system currently copy/ paste only if the names match? If so, it can match the parameter count and input type instead. Then the data can be pasted into any section with same parameter count and data types.
Or keeping the paste button there all the time, and try to fill as many parameters possible if the types match. I don't know if it'll cause any issues though.
